# Verification plan: `irq_ctrl`

- Task: prj-1206fbd80a:dv-plan
- Serves requirement: req-5fc7831312, "Verify the existing interrupt controller RTL."
- Source specification: interface_spec.md (approved artifact prj-1206fbd80a.interface-spec.a1,
  sha256:fb13927a542a48345d42b3507423c39ded9baabfe56889102dd07ab255b18962)
- Status: draft for independent review. No test, assertion or coverage result exists yet.

## 1. Scope and strategy

- Design under test: the existing `irq_ctrl` RTL, a black box. Only its ports are used.
- Features in scope: parameter range, reset, the four registers, level and edge detection,
  clearing, masking, priority, the claim register and combinational output timing.
  Every requirement tag in the spec is in scope (section 6).
- Methods:
  1. Directed tests, one or more per requirement (section 3).
  2. Assertions bound to the DUT ports, active in every test (section 4).
  3. A cycle-accurate reference model with a scoreboard (section 2). It compares
     `rdata`, `irq` and `irq_id` every cycle and, through reads, `PENDING`, `ENABLE`
     and `MODE`.
  4. A constrained-random test, T15, measured against the functional coverage model (section 5).
- Out of scope: physical timing, clock-domain crossing (the spec makes `src` synchronous)
  and power.

## 2. Reference model

The model holds `ENABLE`, `MODE`, `PENDING` (each N bits) and `prev` (N bits, the
remembered source level). It updates them at each rising edge of `clk`:

```
if (!rst_n) { ENABLE = 0; MODE = 0; PENDING = 0; prev = 0; }
else {
  detect = (~MODE & src) | (MODE & src & ~prev);                 // IRQ-LEVEL, IRQ-EDGE, IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED
  clear  = 0;
  if (we && addr == 2) clear = wdata[N-1:0];                     // IRQ-W1C
  if (we && addr == 3 && wdata[4:0] < N) clear = 1 << wdata[4:0]; // IRQ-ACK
  PENDING = (PENDING & ~clear) | detect;                         // IRQ-SET-WINS
  if (we && addr == 0) ENABLE = wdata[N-1:0];                    // IRQ-REG-RW
  if (we && addr == 1) MODE   = wdata[N-1:0];                    // IRQ-REG-RW
  prev = src;
}
```

The outputs are combinational from the current state (IRQ-READ, IRQ-LATENCY):

```
act    = PENDING & ENABLE;
irq    = |act;                                                   // IRQ-MASK
irq_id = irq ? lowest set bit index of act : 0;                  // IRQ-PRIORITY
rdata  = addr==0 ? zext(ENABLE) : addr==1 ? zext(MODE)
       : addr==2 ? zext(PENDING) : {irq, 26'b0, irq_id};         // IRQ-CLAIM, IRQ-PARAM
```

Detection uses `MODE` as it stood before the edge; a `MODE` write takes effect for
detection from the next edge on. This follows from the register semantics and is
recorded as an assumption in section 7.

## 3. Directed tests

Every test runs at each N in the sweep {2, 3, 8, 16, 31, 32}. The default N is 8.

| ID | Name | Stimulus | Checks | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| T01 | reset_values | Load nonzero values into all registers and hold `src` high. Assert `rst_n` for 1 cycle and again for several cycles, including mid-traffic. | `ENABLE`, `MODE`, `PENDING` read 0 after reset. An edge source held high across reset sets `PENDING` at the first edge after reset, because `prev` was cleared. | IRQ-RESET |
| T02 | enable_mode_rw | Write walking-1, walking-0, all-ones and random values to `ENABLE` and `MODE`, then read back. | Readback equals `wdata[N-1:0]`. The other register is unchanged. | IRQ-REG-RW |
| T03 | read_no_side_effect | Read every address repeatedly with `we` low, and change `addr` in the middle of a cycle. | No register changes. `rdata` updates combinationally with `addr`, before any clock edge. | IRQ-READ |
| T04 | level_detect | Set `MODE`=0. Pulse each source for 1 cycle, hold for many cycles, and clear while still high. | `PENDING` is set at every edge where the source is high, so it re-sets after a clear while high. | IRQ-LEVEL |
| T05 | edge_detect | Set `MODE`=1. Single-cycle pulses, a long hold, back-to-back pulses with 1 low cycle, and a high input when `MODE` is switched to 1. | Exactly one set per low-to-high transition. A held-high input does not re-set after a clear. | IRQ-EDGE |
| T06 | detect_disabled | Set `ENABLE`=0 and assert sources in both modes, then enable afterwards. | `PENDING` is set while disabled and `irq` stays low. `irq` rises combinationally when `ENABLE` is written. | IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED, IRQ-MASK |
| T07 | pending_w1c | With all bits pending, write random masks, all-zero, all-ones and masks with bits >= N set, to `PENDING` while sources are idle. | Bits written 1 clear and bits written 0 stay. No bit is ever set by the write. | IRQ-W1C, IRQ-PARAM |
| T08 | claim_ack | Acknowledge each source number 0..31 with others pending. Also set `wdata` bits 31..5 nonzero. | Only the named bit clears. Numbers >= N change nothing. | IRQ-ACK |
| T09 | set_wins | Make detection coincide with a `PENDING` write or a `CLAIM` acknowledge of the same bit, in both modes. Acknowledge a level source while its input is high. | The bit stays set. The level source stays pending and `irq` stays high. | IRQ-SET-WINS |
| T10 | irq_mask | Run all combinations of PENDING x ENABLE for small N, random combinations for large N, in mixed modes. | `irq` == \|(PENDING & ENABLE) every cycle. | IRQ-MASK |
| T11 | priority | Pend sets of sources containing every pair (i, j). Enable subsets. Clear the winner and observe the next winner. | `irq_id` is the lowest pending and enabled index, and 0 when `irq` is low. | IRQ-PRIORITY |
| T12 | claim_read | Read `CLAIM` with `irq` low, with `irq` high, with each `irq_id` value and with source N-1. | `rdata[31]`=`irq` and `rdata[4:0]`=`irq_id`. `rdata[30:5]`=0. | IRQ-CLAIM |
| T13 | latency | Single-cycle source pulse. Then an `ENABLE` write and a `PENDING` clear, each followed by sampling just after the edge. | `irq`/`irq_id` change in the same cycle as the register update, with no extra delay. A source detected at edge k drives `irq` from edge k until the next state change. | IRQ-LATENCY |
| T14 | param_bounds | Write all-ones to `ENABLE`, `MODE` and `PENDING` and drive all `src` bits. Run at N=2 and N=32 (the boundaries) and at the intermediate sweep values. | Bits N..31 read 0 and ignore writes. Behaviour is correct at both bounds. | IRQ-PARAM |
| T15 | random_stress | Constrained-random `src`, `we`, `addr`, `wdata` and `rst_n` (rare), with weighted collisions. At least 100k cycles per N value. | Scoreboard against the section 2 model on every cycle. All assertions pass. | all |

## 4. Assertions

These are written as SVA properties on the DUT ports and checked in every test. The
properties hold internal shadow state from the reference model where needed.

| ID | Property | Requirements |
|---|---|---|
| A01 | After an edge with `!rst_n`: ENABLE, MODE, PENDING read 0 | IRQ-RESET |
| A02 | `we && addr inside {0,1}` implies that register reads `wdata[N-1:0]` next cycle | IRQ-REG-RW |
| A03 | `!we` implies `$stable` of ENABLE, MODE and PENDING except detection-driven sets | IRQ-READ |
| A04 | `rdata` == model rdata(addr) at all times, sampled at the negedge and after `addr` changes | IRQ-READ, IRQ-CLAIM |
| A05 | `rst_n && !MODE[i] && src[i]` implies `PENDING[i]` next cycle | IRQ-LEVEL, IRQ-SET-WINS |
| A06 | `rst_n && MODE[i] && src[i] && !$past(src[i])` implies `PENDING[i]` next cycle | IRQ-EDGE, IRQ-SET-WINS |
| A07 | `PENDING[i]` rises only on a detection, never on a write | IRQ-W1C, IRQ-ACK |
| A08 | Detection is independent of `ENABLE[i]` (A05 and A06 have no `ENABLE` term) | IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED |
| A09 | A `PENDING` write without detection gives PENDING_next == PENDING & ~wdata[N-1:0] | IRQ-W1C |
| A10 | A `CLAIM` write without detection changes at most bit `wdata[4:0]`, and nothing when `wdata[4:0] >= N` | IRQ-ACK |
| A11 | `irq` == \|(PENDING & ENABLE) | IRQ-MASK, IRQ-LATENCY |
| A12 | `irq` implies `irq_id` == lowest set bit of PENDING & ENABLE; `!irq` implies `irq_id` == 0 | IRQ-PRIORITY |
| A13 | Read of `addr`==3 gives `rdata[30:5]` == 0, `rdata[31]` == irq and `rdata[4:0]` == irq_id | IRQ-CLAIM |
| A14 | `rdata[31:N]` == 0 for addr in {0,1,2} | IRQ-PARAM |
| A15 | `irq`/`irq_id` have no `$past` dependence beyond register state, checked by comparison with the combinational model | IRQ-LATENCY |

## 5. Functional coverage

| ID | Cover point / cross | Bins | Requirements |
|---|---|---|---|
| C01 | Parameter N | 2, 3, 8, 16, 31, 32 | IRQ-PARAM |
| C02 | Reset | reset with each register nonzero; reset with `src` high; reset during a write | IRQ-RESET |
| C03 | Write address x data pattern | addr 0..3 x {0, all-ones, walking-1, random, bits >= N set} | IRQ-REG-RW, IRQ-W1C, IRQ-ACK, IRQ-PARAM |
| C04 | Read address x `addr` change without a clock edge | addr 0..3 | IRQ-READ |
| C05 | Per source: mode x src transition | {level, edge} x {0->0, 0->1, 1->1, 1->0} | IRQ-LEVEL, IRQ-EDGE |
| C06 | Per source: detection while disabled | level, edge | IRQ-DETECT-DISABLED |
| C07 | Clear type x collision | {W1C, ACK} x {no detection, same-edge detection} x {level, edge} | IRQ-W1C, IRQ-ACK, IRQ-SET-WINS |
| C08 | ACK number | 0..N-1 each, at least one value >= N (when N < 32) | IRQ-ACK |
| C09 | `irq` toggles caused by | detection, ENABLE write, W1C, ACK, reset | IRQ-MASK, IRQ-LATENCY |
| C10 | `irq_id` value | 0..N-1 each, with at least one lower-numbered pending-but-disabled source | IRQ-PRIORITY |
| C11 | Number of simultaneously active sources | 0, 1, 2, many, all | IRQ-MASK, IRQ-PRIORITY |
| C12 | CLAIM read | irq=0; irq=1 x each irq_id | IRQ-CLAIM |

Coverage target: 100% of the bins above, with no waivers unless a reviewer records one.
Code coverage (line, branch, toggle) on the DUT is collected as a supplementary signal.
Any hole in it is analysed against the requirements, not waived by default.

## 7. Interpretation points

The spec does not state these points. The plan assumes the reading given here, and a test
names each one so that a mismatch with the RTL is visible. A mismatch goes to the
interface spec owner for resolution; it is not resolved in the testbench.

1. Reset priority: at an edge with `rst_n` low, any detection or write at the same edge
   is discarded (T01, C02).
2. CLAIM write upper bits: `wdata` bits 31..5 are ignored on a `CLAIM` write (T08). The
   spec names only bits 4..0.
3. Remembered level: `prev` samples `src` at every non-reset edge regardless of `MODE`.
   A source switched from level to edge mode while high therefore does not trigger again
   (T05).
4. MODE write timing: a `MODE` write at edge k affects detection from edge k+1 (section 2).
5. N = 32: there are no bits >= N, and every ACK number is a valid source. C08 has no
   ">= N" bin at N=32.

## 8. Exit criteria

- All tests T01 to T15 pass at every N in the sweep, with zero scoreboard mismatches.
- All assertions A01 to A15 are enabled and none fires. Each has a non-vacuous cover
  showing its antecedent occurred.
- Functional coverage C01 to C12 is at 100%, or every hole has a recorded waiver from a
  reviewer.
- Every interpretation point in section 7 is confirmed by the RTL or resolved with the
  spec owner.
- The plan passes the platform's vplan.check against the approved interface spec, and an
  independent review is recorded.
